edits.old: Implement the complete box-local contract for M1; M2 adds the external adapter and transport conformance, not a second semantic model. A pure model transition takes state, a validated event and current local monotonic time. Adapters establish event provenance; the model checks supplied boot/session/connection/generation, command freshness and recovery context. Volatile bindings, arms, reservations, motion, challenge times and timer generations never reload as authority. Persist accepted identities/outcomes and versioned service/reconciliation/clear state; historical binding references remain evidence only.

The M0 model defines its own pure nested types and depends on no M1 process, Repo or Games struct. Adapter completion adopts only committed durable changes, never an old volatile state snapshot.

edits.old: Use a thin compiled `Vault.SimulatedBox.Store` over Exqlite/SQLite for the bounded durable subset, with one separate file/connection per box instance outside the server checkpoint. Explicit initialization creates a new store; reopening an expected store never silently replaces missing, corrupt or unsupported history. Run the same protocol-derived traces with literal expected observations through both adapters; agreement between adapters alone is insufficient because the model is shared.

edits.old: **M2-04 — Persistence failure.** Use the initial 100 ms SQLite `busy_timeout`; hold a write lock and separately inject a write failure. Measure a bounded error path targeting less than the 400 ms input lease on the tested machine, without claiming hard real-time guarantees. No success, uncommitted state, or actuator effect may escape. Enter a volatile recovery pause with a `storage_error` diagnostic; retain the committed checkpoint. No transaction waits on the network. Record measured latency and configuration changes. Exercise each independent simulator SQLite store: expected-file missing/corrupt/version refusal, failures before/after commit, lost commit reply and crash/reload. Verify effective durability settings and measured latency without treating the busy timeout as a disk-I/O bound.

edits.old: **M2-05 — Atomic winning transition.** Inject crashes before commit, after commit/before dispatch, and after dispatch/before acknowledgement. Before commit: no solved checkpoint or command. After commit: the restored checkpoint references the same durable `command_id`; no replacement ID or automatic replay. Recovery queries the box and preserves uncertainty when execution cannot be established. Complete commit-before-dispatch/unknown_command and accepted/interrupted recovery through explicit closed_no_replay, Reset and a new simulated round. The old identity/outcome remain, no old-ID redelivery or replacement command for the old solve occurs, and only the new solve creates a new intent.

edits.old: **M2-06 — State separation and reconciliation.** Report `accepted`, `motion_complete`, `position_confirmed`, `uncertain`, and `failed` for the current command. Puzzle phase stays `solved`; neither motor completion nor latch confirmation implies an open lid. A null-command readiness report cannot overwrite persisted release intent. Pending/moving/uncertain outcome disables Pause/Reset until reconciled. Exercise protocol recovery preparation, persistent service inhibit, sealed all-motion evidence, mandatory boot/session fence, explicit host closure and local acknowledgement. Readiness alone cannot close an intent. Test valid terminal results, wrong identity, conflicting historical/current evidence, missing journals and unavailable server records. Inject failed writes/crashes/lost replies at each durable boundary; retry idempotently. Deliver original queued effects/envelopes throughout. Race Close against replacement preparation: only one generation wins, local invalidation alone cannot unseal, and old evidence is rejected. After Begin recovery, deliver a late terminal outcome and assert Reset still requires that recovery's host disposition; terminal observations cannot bypass active recovery. Run the same literal expected recovery traces through both simulator adapters with separate state/store/timing fixtures; expectation generation never invokes the model. Separately terminate transport, box runtime and GameSession and inspect persisted history and modeled-step counts. Adapter agreement alone cannot validate their shared semantics.
